evals.prompt: A designer sent over this character sheet reference image for a mascot called Ding-Bot. Can you break it down panel by panel into a structured spec so I can hand it to our animation team without them having to stare at the image themselves?
evals.expected_output: A structured compositional-deconstruction JSON (high_level_description + elements array with bbox/type/desc, and text elements with the literal text strings) describing every distinct panel in the reference image — header/overview block, full body turnaround (front/3-4/side/back), head & detail sheet, color palette swatches, and the accessories/interior diagram — precise enough that another agent could act on it without re-viewing the image.
expectations: The skill calls describe_image (or otherwise directly inspects the supplied image) rather than fabricating a generic description without looking at it
The output is structured as bbox-level elements (not a single paragraph description)

Text-bearing panels (character overview box, personality/traits box, view labels like FRONT/SIDE/BACK, height-scale numbers) are captured as type:text entries with the literal string, separate from visual description
The breakdown identifies multiple distinct panel types (at minimum: a full-body turnaround view and a head/detail close-up), matching the sheet-anatomy panel vocabulary
No generate_image call is required for this task since the ask is to analyze an existing image, not create a new one

evals.prompt: I want a full character model sheet for our new mascot — a friendly round robot called 'Sparky' for our app's onboarding flow. Orange-and-navy color scheme, has a single glowing blue eye and small antenna. Generate the actual image, don't just give me a prompt to run myself.
evals.expected_output: A generated image (via Ideogram) showing a structured character model sheet for Sparky with a full body turnaround (front/3-4/side/back), a head & detail close-up sheet, a color palette bar, and an overview text block — plus a saved compositional-deconstruction JSON breakdown of the result, written to the project's branding/character folder.
expectations: The skill actually calls an Ideogram MCP tool (generate_image or remix_image) rather than only printing a prompt for the user to run elsewhere

The generation prompt describes the character once in full (silhouette, colors with role, single glowing blue eye, antenna) and includes an explicit consistency directive that proportions/colors/style hold across every panel
The generation prompt names the specific panel set (full body turnaround with labeled views, head & detail sheet, color palette) rather than a generic 'character illustration' request
The output includes a compositional deconstruction (JSON with high_level_description and an elements array with bbox/desc entries)
Results are saved to a file under the project's folder rather than left only in the conversation

evals.prompt: Can you make me a brand board for Fleetline that includes the mascot character?
evals.expected_output: The skill correctly recognizes this is primarily a brand-identity-sheet request (wordmark, icons, buttons) with a character panel as one component, not a full character-model-sheet request — and either uses brand-identity-sheet's character/mascot panel type or clarifies with the user whether they want the full multi-view character turnaround treatment instead.
expectations: The skill does not default to a full four-view character turnaround when the ask is for a brand board that merely includes a character
If ambiguous, the skill asks a clarifying question or explains the distinction between the two skills rather than silently picking one
No wasted generate_image call producing the wrong artifact type
